items.title: Presentation of a Proclamation recognizing Hispanic Heritage Month in Coral Gables.
Official welcome of the Berlin Police Department command staff.
Presentation of a Resolution of Condolence to the family of Operator Tracy Bowen.
Congratulations to Coral Gables Dentistry for receiving the 2026 Keep Coral Gables Beautiful Commercial Beautification Award.
Proclamation declaring October 19-25, 2026, as "Florida City Government Week" in Coral Gables.
Proclamation declaring November 15, 2026, as "America Recycles Day" in Coral Gables.
Recognition of the Fire Department's Commission on Accreditation of Ambulance Services (CAAS) accreditation.
Recognition of Engine 1 and Rescue 1 for their response to an electrocution call.

A Resolution of the City Commission granting the Coral Gables Firefighter Benevolent Association permission to sell Christmas trees, install a temporary chain-link fence, and display an inflatable Santa Claus at Coral Gables Baptist Church, 5501 Granada Boulevard, from November 21, 2026, through December 24, 2026.

A Resolution of the City Commission approving a Fifth Amendment to the lease between the City of Coral Gables and Sollie, LLC, doing business as Haagen Dazs, for 286 Miracle Mile, Coral Gables, Florida 33134, and granting a one-month base rent abatement to offset the tenant's temporary closure during its remodel. Lobbyist: N/A.

An Ordinance of the City Commission providing for a text amendment to the City of Coral Gables Official Zoning Code, Article 5, "Architecture," Section 5-203, "Coral Gables Mediterranean architecture design," to amend the height exclusion requirements to include enclosed areas as accessory uses; providing for a repealer provision, severability clause, codification, and providing for an effective date. (PZB recommended approval 5-0, 09/16/26)

An Ordinance of the City Commission providing for a text amendment to the City of Coral Gables Official Zoning Code, Appendix A, "Site Specific Zoning Regulations," Section A-36, "Crafts Section," to amend the height restriction so that Block 36, Crafts Section, may not receive additional stories or height through architectural incentives; providing for a repealer provision, severability clause, and providing for an effective date. (PZB recommended approval 5-0, 09/16/26)

An Ordinance of the City Commission providing for a text amendment to the City of Coral Gables Official Zoning Code, Article 2, "Zoning Districts," and Article 3, "Uses," to specify a driveway side setback, allow motor courts on corner lots, and adjust rear and side setbacks for certain mechanical equipment; providing for a repealer provision, severability clause, codification, and providing for an effective date. (PZB recommended approval 5-0, 09/16/26)

An Ordinance of the City Commission amending the City Code, Chapter 22, "Emergency Services," Article II, "Burglary, Fire and Robbery Alarms," updating alarm system definitions and requirements, the annual alarm registration requirement and the registration and false alarm fee collection process, and allowing an alternative representative to perform certain requirements on behalf of the Finance Department; providing for a repealer provision, severability clause, codification, and providing for an effective date.

A Resolution of the City Commission directing the City Manager to review and address traffic patterns, valet staging, and parking issues along Caballero Boulevard and Madruga Avenue associated with the Paseo de la Riviera development at 1350 South Dixie Highway, and to work with the property owner and operator to resolve them; providing for an effective date. (Sponsored by Vice Mayor Anderson)

(Sponsored by Mayor Lago)
Presentation of the swale planting package and permit process. (Sponsored by Mayor Lago)
Discussion regarding a permitting roundtable with industry leaders. (Sponsored by Mayor Lago)
Discussion regarding alternative materials for tree protection structures. (Sponsored by Mayor Lago)
Discussion regarding vehicles stopping on primary emergency thoroughfares. (Sponsored by Vice Mayor Anderson)

A Resolution of the City Commission accepting the recommendation of the Chief Procurement Officer to award the Art Cinema Expansion Project to Hycon Investments, LLC, the most responsive and responsible bidder, in an estimated total amount of $1,239,900.00 pursuant to Invitation for Bids (IFB) 2026-021 and Section 2-763 of the Procurement Code entitled "Contract Award." Lobbyist: N/A
items.fiscal: in the estimated total amount of $1,239,900.00 not to exceed the available budget

items.title: A Resolution of the City Commission approving the Fourth Amendment to the amended and restated lease between the City of Coral Gables and the Coral Gables Cinemateque, Inc. for the expansion of the Coral Gables Art Cinema at City-owned property located at 240-260 Aragon Avenue, Coral Gables, Florida, subject to certain conditions.

A Resolution of the City Commission authorizing the City Manager to negotiate and execute an agreement with Tresart, Inc. for acquisition of the artwork "Fin" by Richard Serra (recommendation to deny by the Cultural Development Board approval/denial vote: 4 to 2); and authorizing an amendment to the Fiscal Years 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 amended budgets to recognize as revenue a transfer from the Art in Public Places reserve, and appropriating such funds to put toward the cost of acquisition, installation, and related expenses regarding the artwork.
items.fiscal: Funding for the artwork, transportation, installation and related costs is proposed through the Art Fund, to include $118,801 of the FY25-26 interest accrued in the Art Fund and the Art in Public Places permit payment from City Hall Renovation capital project. The artwork will require a foundation that will be funded separately along with installation, lighting, signage, and landscaping. The cost of annual maintenance will be assessed by a professional conservation team once the artwork is installed.

Have a valid email; gather a current Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax Receipt (if located in the county), Certificate of Incorporation (if applicable), W-9, IRS letter 147C, and the notarized Final Summary pages to attach. Vendor Registration Boot Camp: Thursday Nov. 5, 2026, Coral Reef Branch Library, 9211 Coral Reef Drive, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. (page also lists 1 p.m. to 3 p.m.), free, RSVP online.
levers.rules: "Only registered Suppliers/Vendors can be awarded County contracts." (General Terms and Conditions 1.2(A)). "Bidders must complete the Supplier/Vendor Registration within INFORMS, which is free of any charge" (1.3(A)).
levers.deadline: Before award recommendation; a firm must be fully registered before it can receive a county contract.
levers.source: Vendor Registration page; General Terms and Conditions R26-2 https://www.miamidade.gov/resources/strategic-procurement/documents/general-terms-and-conditions-r26-2.pdf; Boot Camp notice https://www.miamidade.gov/global/news-item.page?Mduid_news=news1712072465878334

levers.how: Log into the Business Management Workforce System (B2G) at https://mdcsbd.gob2g.com/, under Certified Firms select Apply for/Renew Certification, answer eligibility questions, upload the document list, Process each section. SPD Certification Unit 305-375-3111.
levers.rules: Programs SBE-Goods & Services, SBE-A&E, SBE-Construction. Max average gross receipts over past 3 years: GS $8M; A&E $6.5M ($8M for engineering, surveying/mapping, landscape architecture); Construction General $15M, Heavy $12M, Specialty $8M. Max personal net worth per owner $3.5M. Owner/qualifier ownership at least 10% (GS, CON) or 25% (A&E). Active Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax receipt held at least one year; physical location in Miami-Dade County (no virtual offices); one active SBE certification per owner. Goods only: manufacturers up to 100 employees, wholesalers up to 50. Certification lasts three years. Micro tiers under Implementing Order 3-41: Micro Tier 1 "$0 to $750,000;" Micro Tier 2 "$750,000.01 to $2,000,000;" Tier 3 "$2,000,000.01 to $5,000,000" (3-year average gross revenues). Set-asides need "at least three (3) available SBEs": $100,000.01 to $750,000 set aside for Micro Tier 1; $750,000.01 to $2,000,000 for Micro Tier 2; $2,000,000.01 to $5,000,000 for Tier 3. Contracts of $100,000 or less: "Micro Tier 1 or Micro Tier 2 shall automatically receive a ten (10) percent bid preference"; Tier 3 5%. Not set aside: 10% preference for $100,000.01 to $1 million, 5% over $1 million.
levers.deadline: None stated; certification valid three years, renew in B2G.
levers.source: SBE Certification page; Implementing Order 3-41 https://documents.miamidade.gov/ao-io/IO/IO-03-41.pdf (effective Oct 30, 2020). IO 3-41 revenue tiers ($5M cap) differ from the current certification page ($8M GS); both recorded as printed.

levers.how: Submit written questions through INFORMS to the Procurement Contracting Officer named on the solicitation cover, with a copy to the Clerk of the Board at clerkbcc@miamidade.gov. The County answers by addendum.
levers.rules: "Any communication or inquiries, except for clarification of process or procedure already contained in the Solicitation, are to be made in writing to the attention of the Procurement Contracting Officer identified on the front page of the Solicitation via INFORMS with a copy sent to the Clerk of the Board, clerkbcc@miamidade.gov." (1.2(D)(1)). "SPD may issue an addendum in response to any inquiry received prior to Bid opening (Event Time and Date End)" (1.2(D)(2)). Cone of Silence: "all Solicitations, once advertised and until an award recommendation are under the Cone of Silence"; "Written communications, copied to the Clerk of the Board, are permitted at all times." Objections to solicitation terms: "at least two (2) workdays (not less than forty-eight (48) hours) prior to the Bid opening date and hour" (1.2(E)(2)).
levers.deadline: Before bid opening (Event Time and Date End in INFORMS); each solicitation may set an earlier questions deadline.
levers.source: General Terms and Conditions R26-2; Cone of Silence page https://www.miamidade.gov/global/strategic-procurement/procedures-cone-of-silence.page; Code Sec. 2-11.1(t)

levers.how: Pre-bid or pre-proposal conferences are set per solicitation and listed in the INFORMS event and solicitation document (for example, draft RFP EVN0022869 Shelter Management set a pre-proposal conference for March 20, 2026, 10:00 AM via Teams). Register in INFORMS to see the event details; the Cone of Silence Report lists only advertise and due dates.
levers.rules: The General Terms and Conditions R26-2 (sections reviewed through 1.58) contain no general pre-bid conference clause; attendance requirements, if any, are stated in each solicitation.
levers.source: INFORMS Online Bidding System page; draft RFP EVN0022869 https://www.miamidade.gov/Apps/ISD/StratProc/ProcurementNAS/pdf_Files/FutureSolicitations/RFP_Solicitation_EVN-0022869.pdf

levers.how: Contract awards above the Mayor's delegated authority go to the Board of County Commissioners (usually first through a committee). Speak under Rule 6.06 (reasonable opportunity to be heard) by registering at the meeting, or submit written comment to the Clerk of the Board. Commissioners can pull a consent item for individual consideration.
levers.rules: Citizens' Bill of Rights item 5: "any interested person has the right to appear before the Commission." Rule 6.06: registration on the day of the meeting "no less than one-half hour after the publicly noticed time for the meeting to begin"; "no more than two (2) minutes" per speaker unless the presiding officer grants more; 10 minutes total per side per item; if more than five register on one side they may select a representative for up to four minutes; no person more than five minutes total on one agenda. Rule 6.03 (public hearing items): register "at least fifteen (l5) minutes prior to the commencement of the discussion"; Rule 6.04: "the statement on a public hearing item shall be limited to five (5) minutes." Rule 5.05(a)(1): "Agenda items, including consent agenda items, not selected for individual consideration may be approved in a single vote"; commissioners may "identify certain items for individual consideration (i.e., the 'pull list')." Rule 5.05(c) 4-DAY RULE: "A copy of each agenda item shall be furnished to the members of the commission not later than four (4) working days" before a vote.
levers.deadline: Register at the meeting within the first half hour after the noticed start time (Rule 6.06).
levers.source: BCC Rules of Procedure (Clerk of the Board) and the 2019-02-05 version at https://www.miamidade.gov/commission/library/2019-02-05-rules-of-procedure.pdf

levers.how: Submit and track requests through the county public records portal (GovQA) at https://miamidadecounty.govqa.us/WEBAPP/_rs/RequestSelect.aspx, or contact the department records custodian listed on the public records page. Request the solicitation file, evaluation committee score sheets, tabulations and the committee audio recording by solicitation number.
levers.rules: Chapter 119, Florida Statutes applies. You do not have to give your name or a reason. Online card payment is "temporarily discontinued"; pay at offices. Implementing Order 3-34: "All Committee proceedings shall be audiotaped." Ordinance file 261367 (public hearing 9-1-26) directs committee members to "articulate the rationale(s) for their scoring" and permits "recorded oral presentations before selection committees" under a Florida Statutes exemption.
levers.deadline: None; sealed bids and proposals are exempt until notice of intended decision or 30 days after opening under state law (not printed on the county page).

levers.how: File a written intent to protest with the Clerk of the Board (8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday to Friday) within three working days of the award recommendation being filed, with copies to each bidder/proposer and the County Attorney; file the protest itself with documents and evidence within three working days after that, with the nonrefundable filing fee.
levers.rules: "A participant in any competitive process wishing to file a 'formal' or 'informal' bid protest" may do so (IO 3-21); protests cover awards over $25,000. Formal (over $250,000): intent "within three (3) working days of the filing of the award recommendation with the Clerk of the Board"; then "Within three (3) working days of the filing of the written intent to protest, the protester shall file the bid protest." Informal ($25,001 to $250,000): "within three (3) working days of the posting of the award recommendation." Filing fee: $25,001 to $250,000 $500; $250,001 to $500,000 $1,000 plus $500 administrative fee; $500,001 to $5 million $3,000 plus $1,500; over $5 million $5,000 plus $2,500. Certified SBE protesters pay 50% on SBE set-aside contracts. Administrative fee retained if the hearing examiner finds the protest frivolous. Hearing examiner appointed within 5 working days; hearing within 10 working days; findings within 5 working days; two hours per side. No bond beyond the filing fee is stated.
levers.deadline: Three working days after the award recommendation is filed or posted; three more working days for the full protest.
levers.source: Implementing Order 3-21; Bid Protest page https://www.miamidade.gov/global/strategic-procurement/bid-protest.page; Code Sec. 2-8.4

levers.how: Report fraud, waste, abuse of power or mismanagement to the Office of the Inspector General: online form https://miamidadecounty.co1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0JSHnLek0L3LjE1, 24-hour fraud hotline 305-579-2593, office 305-375-1946 (Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.), or write to 601 NW 1st Court, Transit Village South Tower, 22nd Floor, Miami, FL 33136.
levers.rules: "you may remain anonymous if you wish." If you give your name and ask that your identity not be released, the OIG will protect it to the maximum extent of the law; whistleblower identity stays confidential after case closure. "Under Florida law, e-mail addresses are public records."
